final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest escape score (0.901) via PNGS loss at position 459, with the second-best plausibility among high-escape N->D candidates, balancing escape gain against replication fitness.
Top-tier escape (0.895) with the best plausibility among high-escape glycan-loss mutants; V4 PNGS loss is a well-tolerated, classic escape route.
Strong escape (0.893) with weaker plausibility (0.028), ranked below the two with similar escape but better predicted fitness.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence already ranks the top tier decisively; remaining budget unlikely to change the final Top-3.

history.rationale: Removes a conserved N-glycan sequon (N136-I137-T138) in the V1 region, a classic immune-shield modulation route; glycan loss can expose/reshuffle epitopes while Gln preserves side-chain polarity and folding.
Removes the V1 hypervariable-loop glycan, a classic broadly neutralizing antibody shielding site; loss likely increases escape with modest fitness cost as Gln preserves hydrogen bonding.
Only moderate escape (0.787) and near-zero plausibility (0.004); dominated by other candidates.

rejection.reason: Only moderate escape (0.787) and near-zero plausibility (0.004); dominated by other candidates.

history.rationale: Abolishes the N300-N301-T302 glycan sequon at the base of V3, a known antibody-evasion lever; Asp mimics a deamidated Asn with minimal structural disruption.
Removes a conserved V3-base glycan implicated in bNAb (e.g., PGT128-class) recognition; Asp conserves size/charge character while eliminating the glycan.
Lowest plausibility (0.001) with only moderate escape (0.778); likely replication cost.

rejection.reason: Lowest plausibility (0.001) with only moderate escape (0.778); likely replication cost.

history.rationale: Removes the N361-S362-S363 glycan near the V3 stem region, potentially altering glycan-shield-dependent neutralization sensitivity while keeping the loop fold intact.
Outer-domain glycan near CD4bs bNAb epitopes; glycan loss plausibly increases escape but this glycan is fairly conserved, so fitness cost is a concern.
Escape (0.786) not competitive with top group and plausibility low (0.028).

rejection.reason: Escape (0.786) not competitive with top group and plausibility low (0.028).

history.rationale: Removes the N403-S404-T405 sequon in the V4 region, a variable, escape-prone area where glycan shifts frequently mediate antibody escape without major fitness cost.
Glycan in the CD4bs/V4 region targeted by bNAbs; removal could aid escape, with moderate conservation risk.
Strong escape (0.893) but weak plausibility (0.028); ranked below the two with similar escape and better plausibility.
Disrupts the N459-S460-T461 glycan site in V4, altering local shielding and epitope presentation in a hypervariable, escape-tolerant region.
V5-region glycan shield site; removal may expose epitopes, with plausibility to be checked.
Highest EVEscape (0.901) with the second-best plausibility among N->D candidates (0.049); PNGS loss is a classic escape route but plausibility is low, so confidence stays moderate.
Removes the N151-M152-T153 glycan in C2; glycan repositioning in this region is a documented escape mechanism, though conservation may carry some fitness cost.
V1 glycan removal candidate; plausible escape gain but lower priority than N136.
Good escape (0.866) but very low plausibility (0.006) suggests fitness cost; kept as reserve.
Abolishes the N184-N185-S186 sequon within the variable V1/V2-associated glycan cluster, potentially changing bNAb access while retaining loop structure.
V2-region glycan candidate; escape potential uncertain pending evidence.
By far the best plausibility (0.408) but lowest escape (0.738); retained as fitness-safe fallback.
Removes the N87-V88-T89 glycan in C1; C1 glycan changes can modulate trimer conformation and antibody recognition, but proximity to conserved core raises fitness risk.
C1-region glycan; removal may perturb folding near conserved core, so lower confidence.
Weakest combination: escape 0.765, plausibility 0.001.
Removes the N396-T397-S398 sequon in V4; glycan loss in this variable loop is a plausible escape route with limited impact on the conserved trimer core.
V4 glycan removal candidate near antibody epitopes; needs plausibility/escape evidence.
Top-tier escape (0.895) and the best plausibility among high-escape N->D mutants (0.058); V4 glycan loss generally tolerable.
Charge reversal at the V3 base near the RKSIRI motif can perturb V3-directed antibody binding, but V3 base residues are functionally important so fitness risk is higher.
Charge reversal in V3-base region as a non-glycan escape alternative; kept as diversity hedge.
Decent escape (0.855) with low plausibility (0.008); V3-region charge change, uncertain fitness.
